newsitem.title: USA: Southern, Vastar form electric, gas venture.
newsitem.headline: Southern, Vastar form electric, gas venture.

text.p: Southern Co. is teaming up with a Houston natural gas company in a joint venture expected to form a foundation for its push into deregulated electric and natural gas markets, the companies said Tuesday.

The Atlanta-based utility holding company will pay $40 million for a 60 percent stake in the venture with Vastar Resources Inc. The venture will combine Southern's electric wholesale marketing operations with Vastar's gas marketing arm, the companies said.
"This joint venture would be the generating, supply arm for retail, if it emerges," Marce Fuller, Southern Co. Energy Marketing LP chief executive officer, said.
The venture would have marketed a combined 4 billion cubic feet of gas a day and 6.5 million megawatt hours of electricity last year, ranking it in the top 10 among power marketers nationwide.

Southern expects the venture to rank among the top five in energy marketers by the turn of the century, and will focus initially on U.S. wholesale and large industrial customers as regulators debate opening the nation's electric grid to retail competition.

By 2002, as wholesale and retail markets are opened, the company expects to market up to 10 billion cubic feet a day of gas and 1 trillion megawatt hours of electricity a year, said Joe Pokalsky, a managing director of the venture.

Electricity sales are expected to grow briskly as regulations in the market are lifted. Only about 5 percent of the wholesale electric market is opened to competition and retail markets in the $210 billion industry are set to open next year, beginning in California and New England.
In the deal, Vastar also dedicated "substantially all" of its gas production base to the venture under a 10-year supply agreement, executives said at a news conference.

Terms of the deal were still being ironed out, but the partners expected to begin jointly marketing gas on Sept. 1. The power marketing operations should begin by Jan. 1, 1998, following regulatory approval, Fuller said.
Southern will continue to operate an electric trading floor in Atlanta and Vastar will trade gas out of Houston.
Southern stock fell 25 cents to $62.50 in consolidated trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
